pages.text: Scientists worked across the Overworld before you, and their field sites still stand - built, like the old observatory ruins, from the mod's own materials, with Containment Caches of what they left behind.

$(thing)Survey Benchmarks$() - a neutronium pillar topped with a Cherenkov lamp - stand in every kind of land. $(thing)Observatories$() keep their cracked field-glass domes high in the mountains, a telescope still aimed through the slit.

$(thing)Crashed Satellites$() lie in scorched rings on plains, savannas, deserts and badlands. $(thing)Magnetic Anomaly Sites$() are rare: standing stones of magnetite round a buried knot of it, which the Gauss Meter reads from well away.
$(thing)Fallout Shelters$() are sealed, lead-lined rooms deep underground, lit by radium lamps. They have no door to the surface: a Seismograph, which reports caves below it, is the way to find one.
Some villages keep a $(thing)Probability Hall$(): a floor of Chance Tiles, a Galton Board to study and a cache of dice and tablets.

The sites' blocks can be made too: $(item)Magnetite$() and $(item)Lead$() bricks, Lead Hazard Panels, Radium Lamps, Chance Tiles, and a $(item)Decorative Telescope$() and $(item)Satellite Wreck$() - decoration only; working instruments come later.
